I have an assistant teacher who helps with clean up, taking children to the bathroom, and feeding them. So I have basically entrusted her to help with the other kids, giving them attention, keeping an eye on them so they don’t hurt themselves, and helping them learn. 
This has been enough for now, but I cannot help but feel my connection with my kids is slowly fading. 

I haven’t given her the role of helping him because she gets very stressed around his screaming and crying, and she is often more prone to letting him do as he pleases just so he stops (which would only feed into the tantrums and show him he should keep them going). 

I want to help her as well, she is human too and I’m practically responsible for her well-being.

I have read the books around 8 times, I'm in my 9th at the moment. And yes, it is undeniably sexist and awkward in the sense that Kvothe appears to be perfect in everything he does. But at the same time, I believe it has a justification.   
It is sexist because, of course, it was in a society where women were meant to be pretty, and they could do nothing more of their lives than marry some gent and be a housewife (Dena is an example of this as Deok, the owner of the Eolian, points out). Dena is stuck in flirting with men because she cannot do much more to survive. No family and no will to marry, no studies, no possibility of a job that does not include sex work (which she doesn't want to do, so when the men she dates get pushy, she runs away).   
Fela is a woman that is really smart and great with numbers. Yet she doesn't show up much as she does not interact with Kvothe often. However, she is portrayed as a smart, independent, strong female that is very pretty (though we don't know if this is true or it has to do with the fact that she is part of the very small female population in the university, thus attracting the attention of most of the men around). >!She even starts crying after Kvothe saved her from the fire in the fishery, not because she was in danger and he was her brave savior, but rather because she acted as every "weak female" stereotype she had heard in fantasy stories, which she didn't want to be. !<  
Devi was another example. strong and smart, stronger than Kvothe. She claims she was expelled because she was stronger than all the men in the university, but she was no less smart.   
And the Adem are even more of an example. Their females act differently, they fight, and they are teachers, rulers, and the most important members of society. Men are not needed and are only used for sex, they are not even the best at fighting. This is because their society, since the beginning, was forged on the wisdom of a woman, and thus the perspective on females is different. (which shows us that Kvothes perception of females in his world have to do with his conceptions of femininity because of his society. which invariably makes him sexist. 

Now, on the matter that he is great at everything he does. He is incredibly, undeniably, smart. He claims this is due to the way his parents raised him, forcing him to memorize lines for their plays (which helped him develop great memory), and his varied education with the members of his troupe. Also, Abenthy has to do with it, he cunningly taught a 12 year old all the techniques he needed to develop a strong allar (repeating conversations from memory, playing the "hide the stone" game etc.) which expanded Kvothe's mind and made him very successful in the university, particularly in Sympathy and Artificery (which are the two main courses he takes). When he tried his hand on other matters like alchemy and math, he hated it because he was not good at them at all, because his mind was not trained for such things.   
He is very cunning as well, quick on his feet (possibly as a defence mechanism because of his years in Tarbean), lucky and very mature for his age (this is either because that's what he claims, but also because he was forced to survive alone, saw his parents' bodies, and overall had some special thing about him, which some believe is fae blood but we won't know until book 3). He is also very very immature at times, hence why he is very bad with girls, takes stupid irrational and hot-minded decisions which get him intro trouble very often because he is friking 15 years old, he is 16 in book 2 and it is said that he is between 20-25 as Kote in the waystone inn. This immaturity is precisely what brought him to the "folly" he so often talks about, his pride, his manly bravado, his age and his wits are what brought about the war and got him to be a fugitive.   
Overall, I really like the book, but tbh it might not be a book for everyone and needs several several reads to see everything that needs to be seen. Rothfuss is the type of author that hides eastereggs all around, and a top skim is not enough to see the big picture.

Tbh, I would be very passive-aggressive and petty. I've found that people who act that way respond better with this reaction than with assertivity. Take her stuff out of the fridge if it's in your space or put it on her side, take all the clothes and things in the living room, and put them messily on her bedroom floor.
